Desc_short: This course provides a comprehensive and structured introduction to the field of Aerial Robotics, designed for students looking to build a strong technical foundation in autonomous aerial systems. Grounded in both theory and practical application, it covers the full pipeline from flight mechanics to intelligent autonomy.
Desc:
This course provides a comprehensive and structured introduction to the field of Aerial Robotics, designed for students looking to build a strong technical foundation in autonomous aerial systems. Grounded in both theory and practical application, it covers the full pipeline from flight mechanics to intelligent autonomy.

Over the course, you'll:
✅ Master quadrotor dynamics & 3D control theory
✅ Work with MATLAB simulations
✅ Dive into SLAM & autonomous navigation with A*
✅ Explore swarm robotics & multi-agent coordination

students who successfully complete the course earn the opportunity to take part in a hands-on hardware phase where they get to build and fly a real aerial system, putting every concept they've learned directly into practice.
Evaluation:
Attendance in Speaker sessions (A%)
Weekly Assignments (B%)
Capstone Project (C%)
Passing Criteria: 75% attendance in sessions and weekly assignments
Certification: 75% attendance in sessions and weekly assignments
Week 1: Week 1 - An introduction to quadrotor flight, MATLAB basics & 1D control systems. Students familiar with PID controllers, explore system dynamics through simulations & tackle motor selection and thrust-to-weight ratio analysis.
Week 2: Week 2 - A deep dive into quadrotor kinematics and dynamics — covering Euler angles, rotation matrices, the 12-state state vector, equations of motion & the Newton-Euler formulation. Students simulate quadrotor agility and stopping distance using MATLAB.
Week 3: Week 3 - Development of 2D and 3D linear controllers for the quadrotor. Topics include nested feedback loops, trajectory tracking, hover control, PD/PID controller design & MATLAB-based simulation of full 3D quadrotor control.
Week 4:
Week 4 - Introduction to autonomous navigation — covering Pose Graph SLAM, loop closure, path planning algorithms (A* and RRT) & an overview of swarm robotics and multi-agent coordination.

By the end of the course - Students will have built a solid foundation in quadrotor dynamics, control theory & autonomous navigation, backed by practical MATLAB simulations and assignments — qualifying them for the hands-on hardware implementation phase.

School Name: The Science Summer School (Pure Sciences like Maths, Biology, Physics, Chemistry, Economics*)
Desc_short: Ever wondered what happens inside a chemical reaction — at the level of atoms and electrons — before it shows up in your test tube? Computational chemistry lets you simulate molecules on a computer, predict how they behave, and even discover new materials and drugs without lifting a pipette.
Desc:
This 4-week course is your invitation into that world. No prior background needed — just curiosity. We start from Newton's laws (yes, the same F = ma you've known since school) and build up to running real simulations of molecules using tools that researchers at IITs, MIT, and pharma giants use every day.
This course offers a hands-on introduction to computational chemistry — the art of using computers to understand and predict the behaviour of molecules, materials, and reactions. We will not drown in equations. Instead, we'll focus on why each method exists, when to use it, what its limitations are, and how to actually run a simulation yourself. Every week ends with you doing something on a computer, not just listening.
Evaluation: A=20 B=40 C=40 passing criteria will be 60%
Certification: Passing criteria will be 60% overall score
Week 1:
Week 1 — Energy, Geometry, and students First Simulation
We dive straight into the central idea: every molecule's behaviour is governed by its Potential Energy Surface (PES) — a landscape where valleys are stable structures and hills are transition states. We'll cover what coordinates matter (bond length, angle, dihedral), why finding a minimum on this surface means finding a real molecule, and the difference between local and global minima. We'll introduce optimization algorithms conceptually — steepest descent, conjugate gradient — so you know what's happening when you click "Run." Hands-on: Build water, methane, and ethane on WebMO. Optimize them. Compare the energies. Examine what changes when you start from a bad initial geometry vs a good one. First taste of "computers don't solve problems — people do."
Week 2:
Week 2 — Molecular Mechanics: Treating Atoms Like Balls and Springs
We model bonds as springs (Hooke's law), bending as angular springs, torsion as periodic functions, and atoms repelling/attracting through simple potentials (Lennard-Jones, Coulomb). Together these make a force field — a recipe for calculating the energy of any molecular arrangement. We'll discuss popular force fields (AMBER, CHARMM, OPLS, UFF — the ones that power drug design today), what each is good at, and where they break down. We'll also cover parameterization: where do those k, R₀, ε values actually come from? Hands-on: Optimize butane and watch its torsional energy curve. Compute the energy difference between staggered and eclipsed conformations — and compare your answer to the experimental ~3 kcal/mol. Try the same molecule under two different force fields and explain why the answers differ.
Week 3:
Week 3 — Molecular Dynamics: Making Atoms Move
Force fields tell you energy at a frozen snapshot. But molecules are never static — they wiggle, vibrate, diffuse, react. Molecular Dynamics (MD) gives every atom a velocity, applies Newton's F = ma, and evolves the system in time. We'll cover the integration algorithm (Verlet) intuitively, what a "timestep" means and why femtoseconds, ensembles (NVE, NVT, NPT — what they mean physically), temperature and pressure control, and how MD helps you escape local minima to find the global one. We'll also discuss what MD measures: diffusion coefficients, radial distribution functions, conformational sampling. Hands-on: Run a short MD simulation of liquid water in LAMMPS. Compute the density. Compute the O–O radial distribution function. Compare with experimental values.
Week 4:
Week 4 — The Quantum Leap: Why Electrons Matter + DFT Intuition
Force fields can't break or form bonds (they have no electrons!). For chemistry — actual reactions, charge transfer, spectra — we need quantum mechanics. We'll conceptually introduce the Schrödinger equation, the Born–Oppenheimer approximation (why nuclei and electrons get separated), and the basic idea of Density Functional Theory (DFT) — the workhorse of modern computational chemistry. No solving integrals; just the idea — that the electron density tells you everything, and that exchange-correlation functionals (LDA, GGA, hybrid) are different "recipes" with different trade-offs. We'll briefly contrast MM vs DFT in terms of cost, accuracy, and what they can answer. Hands-on: A guided DFT calculation on a small molecule (H₂O or CH₄) using a free, browser-accessible tool — optimize geometry, get the energy, compute vibrational frequencies.

Project
The Project: Pick a small molecule of your choice (3–10 heavy atoms — examples we'll provide: ethanol, formaldehyde, acetic acid, glycine, benzene, water dimer). Then carry out a multi-method comparative study on it.

By the end of this project student can learn
Understand what computational chemistry can and cannot do
Know the difference between Molecular Mechanics, Molecular Dynamics, and Quantum Mechanical methods — and why each exists
Be able to read a research paper that uses simulations and follow the methodology section
Have personally run optimizations, MD simulations, and a basic DFT calculation
Be confident enough to pick this up further on your own — through MOOCs, papers, or a research project

Course Name: Simulation and Optimisation of Smart Energy Systems
Desc_short: A practical and technology-oriented introduction to modern energy systems with emphasis on renewable energy integration, computational simulation, optimisation techniques, smart grid technologies, IoT-enabled energy monitoring, and AI-based intelligent energy management systems.
Desc: The course combines sustainability concepts with modern computational tools, including Python, linear programming, and data-driven approaches, to address next-generation energy infrastructure.
Evaluation: Grading Format - 4 quizzes, each with 25% weightage.
Certification: Passing Criteria: Minimum 50% overall score across all quizzes. Participants must attempt at least 3 out of 4 weekly quizzes to complete the course.
Week 1: Week 1 — Fundamentals of Modern Energy Systems. Students will be introduced to the evolution of conventional and smart energy systems, including the integration of renewable energy technologies such as solar and wind power. The week also covers energy demand patterns, load profiles, grid challenges, and the need for simulation and optimisation in modern energy infrastructure.
Week 2: Week 2 — Simulation and Computational Modelling. This week focuses on computational modelling and simulation techniques used in energy systems. Students will learn the basics of Python and Google Colab, model solar and battery systems, understand battery State of Charge (SOC), and analyse energy datasets using Pandas and Matplotlib for visualisation and interpretation of simulation results.
Week 3: Week 3 — Optimisation of Energy Systems. Students will explore optimisation techniques used in energy management and sustainable power systems. Topics include optimisation fundamentals, objective functions, constraints, energy scheduling, peak demand reduction, battery management, and linear programming using tools such as SciPy Optimise and PuLP. A hands-on activity on battery scheduling optimisation will also be included.
Week 4:
Week 4 — Smart Energy Technologies and Future Systems. The final week introduces emerging technologies transforming the energy sector, including smart grids, IoT-enabled monitoring systems, EV charging infrastructure, intelligent energy management, AI applications in energy systems, digital twins, and data-driven analytics for future sustainable energy solutions.

By the End of the Course: Students will gain foundational knowledge of modern energy systems, renewable energy integration, and smart grid technologies. They will develop hands-on skills in Python-based simulation, energy data analysis, and optimisation techniques, while also exploring emerging technologies such as IoT, EV infrastructure, and AI-driven energy systems.

School Name: The Science Summer School (Pure Sciences like Maths, Biology, Physics, Chemistry, Economics*)
Desc_short: The course bridges engineering and markets through logical optimization puzzles. Over four weeks, you will dissect counterintuitive paradoxes.
Desc: From how free solar power crashes electricity prices to why energy efficiency can increase fuel consumption.
Certification: Evaluation criteria: 1) Attempted atleast 3 quizzes 2) more than 40% in quizzes
Week 1: Week 1 — Macro Energy Dynamics and Resource Horizons. Students will explore the economics of finite energy resources and consumer behaviour in energy markets. Topics include resource depletion strategies, Hotelling’s Rule, the Green Paradox, energy efficiency gaps, and Jevon’s Paradox, providing insight into how energy markets and human behaviour shape long-term energy consumption.
Week 2: Week 2 — Power Grid Operations and Market Regulations. This week focuses on electricity market structures and grid economics. Students will learn how grid auctions determine electricity prices, how transmission networks operate under physical constraints, and how concepts such as merit order curves, uniform price auctions, locational marginal pricing, and regulatory monopolies influence modern power systems.
Week 3: Week 3 — Clean Energy Economics and the Solar Paradox. Students will analyse the economic and operational challenges introduced by renewable energy integration. The course covers net load profiles, the duck curve, renewable energy subsidies, renewable cannibalisation, and the missing money problem, helping students understand the complexities of maintaining stable and profitable clean energy markets.
Week 4:
Week 4 — Grid Flexibility, Storage, and Decarbonisation Policy. The final week explores energy storage economics, battery arbitrage, grid flexibility, and long-term decarbonisation strategies. Students will study how future grid assets generate value through revenue stacking, manage capital risk, and support reliable low-carbon energy systems.

By the End of the Course: Students will gain a strong understanding of energy market economics, power grid operations, renewable energy integration, and energy storage systems. They will develop the ability to analyse electricity markets, understand policy and pricing mechanisms, and evaluate the economic forces driving the global clean energy transition.

1. Building an AI-powered assistant application
2. Prompting and customizing cloud-hosted LLMs
3. Introduction to RAG-based assistants
4. Creating interfaces using Streamlit or Gradio
5. Deploying and demonstrating AI applications
6. Overview of advanced AI topics like (Reinforcement Learning, Stable Diffusion, DPO/PPO, Agentic AI, SSMs)

By the end of the course participants will be able to understand the fundamentals of ML and AI, work with Python ML libraries, and deploy applications.

School Name: The Science Summer School (Pure Sciences like Maths, Biology, Physics, Chemistry, Economics*)
Desc_short: The Quantum Circuits course breaks down the heart of quantum computers, shows how computation happens, and teaches you to build a decomposition algorithm which turns a matrix into a circuit of logic gates.
Desc: This is extremely important today because every quantum computer from Google's to IBM's has a limited set of gates to work with, and this algorithm addresses that.
Certification: Passing criteria: 40%. Subject to change depending on student performance.
Pre-req: Some experience in coding in Python is welcome, but not required.
Week 1: Week 1 - Intro to quantum computing, qubits, and circuits.
Week 2: Week 2 - Mathematics of a universal gate set & circuit synthesis.
Week 3: Week 3 - Implementing a quantum circuit compiler.
Week 4:
Week 4 - Using the compiler to simulate Grover’s Algorithm. Test how many qubits a laptop can simulate.

By the end of the course - You will have learnt the nitty-gritties of how quantum computers compute, worked with the intricate math behind quantum logic gates, and written an algorithm to decompose a circuit into logic gates.

School Name: The Science Summer School (Pure Sciences like Maths, Biology, Physics, Chemistry, Economics*)
Desc_short: Ever wondered why people make the choices they do, in negotiations, competitions, or even everyday decisions? Game Theory gives you the mathematical tools to actually understand and predict strategic behaviour.
Desc: Over this course, you will learn what it even means to be "rational", and build your way up through some of the most elegant ideas in economics and mathematics. You'll explore classic dilemmas, learn how to find Nash Equilibria, and even get into the fascinating world of mixed strategies and incomplete information. By the end, you'll be looking at everything from chess to auctions to politics in a completely different light.
Certification: Passing Criteria=60%
Week 1: Week 1: Why game theory, the game of chess, introduction to normal form games (Prisoner's Dilemma), Idea of Rationality
Week 2: Week 2: Model of Normal form games, Concept of domination, WDSE, SDSE, Nash equilibrium, PSNE,
Week 3: Week 3: Concept of Mixed Strategy, Idea of MSNE, Existence and Computation of MSNEs, Bayesian games/games with imperfect info
Week 4: Week 4: Extensive form games, behavioral strategies and kuhn's theorem, stochastic extensive form games

School Name: The Science Summer School (Pure Sciences like Maths, Biology, Physics, Chemistry, Economics*)
Desc_short: Several processes in nature are out of equilibrium, as such, they can not be modeled within the framework of regular thermodynamics/statistical physics.
Desc: This course seeks to introduce the learner to interesting out of equilibrium phenomenon like brownian motion and diffusion by looking for the statistical laws that govern them. Through this, the learner will also gain some perspective on how random processes are studied.
Certification: Passing Criteria=TBD
Week 1: Week 1 : Basics of probability and classical statistical mechanics (Kolmogorovs axioms, PDFs, moments, cumulants, conditional probability, probability in classical stat mech, microcanonical and canonical ensemble, statistical mechanics from the feynman lectures)
Week 2: Week 2 : The Chapmann Kolmogorov equation, Master equation for jump processes, Diffusion and Birth-Death processes as examples, Transition rates from the hamiltonian, detailed balance, continuum limit of the master equation
Week 3: Week 3 : Langevin dynamics, gaussian white noise, OU process, fluctuation - dissipation relation, relation to Fokker-Planck equations
Week 4: Week 4 : Basic simulations (Kinetic Monte Carlo for the master equation and additive noise for Langevin)

School Name: The Sports and Skills Summer School
Desc_short: Transform your funny everyday thoughts into stage-ready stand-up comedy with this practical masterclass.
Desc:
By balancing joke writing secrets with performance psychology, you will learn to build a clear stage persona, write high-laugh routines, and easily control live crowd energy. From making your first 5-minute set to mastering timing, this course gives you the hands-on tools and muscle memory needed to own any stage with total confidence.

This course offers an intensive, step-by-step deep dive into the art and craft of stand-up comedy. Designed to transform your spontaneous, funny thoughts and everyday stories into polished, stage-ready material, this curriculum balances foundational joke mechanics with professional performance psychology.
Certification: passing Criteria(75%)
Week 1: Week 1:- The opening week provides a comprehensive structural overview of comedy, introducing the core building blocks of joke writing and exploring diverse comedic styles so you can discover the specific sub-genre that best suits your natural voice.
Week 2: Week 2:- Week two shifts focus from isolated joke mechanics to structural architecture. You will learn how to seamlessly weave jokes into an extended, high-engagement bit and master the subtle writing theories that professional comics use to maximize stage energy.
Week 3: Week 3:- Week three introduces advanced comedic theory, teaching you how to engineer highly sophisticated joke structures, navigate the emotional boundaries of an audience, and strategically manipulate live room energy.
Week 4:
Week 4:- The final week transitions from the text to the physical space of the stage, focusing heavily on character alignment, the psychology of live performance, objective self-documentation, and professional career sustainability.

By the end of this course, you will transform spontaneous funny thoughts into structured, stage-ready stand-up routines by mastering advanced mechanics like misdirection, Word Smuggling, and the Seesaw Theory.

School Name: The Sustainability Summer School
Desc_short: Sustainable Policies 101 is a beginner-friendly course that introduces you to the world of environmental governance from global climate negotiations to how local municipalities manage waste.
Desc: Across four weeks, you'll explore the institutions, policies, principles, and real-world case studies that shape environmental decision-making at every level. Whether you're curious about COPs, carbon markets, or how your city plans for sustainability, this course connects the dots between climate science and climate action in a language you can relate to.
Certification: Completion of assignments and project benchmarks.
Week 1: Week 1: Introduction to Environmental Policy & Governance
Week 2: Week 2: Environmental Governance in India
Week 3: Week 3: Global Climate Policy & International Agreements
Week 4:
Week 4: Urban, Local, and Future-Ready Environmental Policy

By the end of this course - you will be able to understand how environmental policies are designed and implemented at local, national, and global levels. You’ll gain the ability to analyze key climate agreements, interpret sustainability policies, evaluate real-world environmental challenges, and connect governance frameworks with practical climate action.

School Name: The CS and DS Summer School
Desc_short: This course is a beginner-friendly introduction to full stack web development, designed to help students build modern web applications from scratch.
Desc: Participants will learn the fundamentals of programming, frontend and backend development, databases, deployment, and software engineering practices through hands-on learning and practical assignments. By the end of the course, students will create and deploy their own web application with creative features and real-world functionality.

School Name: The CS and DS Summer School
Desc_short: Every business runs on data, but most of it is locked inside websites, messy spreadsheets, and scattered systems. The people who can pull it out, clean it up, store it properly, and turn it into a dashboard are the ones companies actually pay for.
Desc: This bootcamp will make you go from your first line of Python to shipping a complete data pipeline: scrape real data from the web, analyze it in Excel, query it with SQL, store it in PostgreSQL, and visualize it in Power BI.
Certification: Passing Criteria 2 or 3 assignments and 1 capstone project
Week 1:
Week 1: Web Scraping & Data Retrieval Methods
Learn where data actually comes from. Understand how websites and APIs work, write your first Python scripts to pull real data from the web. By the end of the week you'll have scraped your own dataset that you'll keep building on for the rest of the bootcamp.
Week 2:
Week 2: Excel Fundamentals
Everyone thinks they know Excel. Almost no one actually does. The difference between dragging cells around for hours and finishing the same work in ten minutes comes down to a handful of formulas most people have never touched.
Week 3:
Week 3: SQL & Querying Data
Excel breaks at a million rows. SQL doesn't. Learn the single most valuable skill in data work: querying databases. Filter, group, join, and aggregate data to answer real business questions, using SQLite.
Week 4:
Week 4: PostgreSQL & Power BI Dashboarding
Graduate from a learning database to a production one. Set up PostgreSQL, load your data properly, then connect it to Power BI to build interactive dashboards with filters, KPIs, and visuals stakeholders can actually use.

School Name: The CS and DS Summer School
Desc_short: Every company is racing to automate with AI  and the people who can build it are the most in-demand.
Desc: In 4 weeks you will go from your first LLM API call to shipping a fully autonomous multi-agent workflow. The same architecture powering the most advanced AI products in production today. Prompt engineering. RAG. LangChain. LangGraph. Real APIs. Real projects. No ML background required. The only question is whether you build this now or watch others do it.
Certification: 2 out of 3 assignments and 1 capstone project are compulsory for certification
Week 1:
Week 1: Understanding LLMs: Prompting & APIs
Learn how LLMs work, why prompt structure matters, and how to move from chatting in a browser to controlling a model through.
Week 2:
Week 2: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) & Fine Tunning
Teach your LLM to answer from your own documents using RAG, and learn when fine-tuning makes more sense.
Week 3:
Week 3: Agentic AI (MCPs, LangChain, LangGraph)
Go from generating text to taking action. Build an agent that can use tools, make decisions, and execute multi-step tasks using LangChain, LangGraph, and MCP.
Week 4:
Week 4: Multi Agent Workflows and Capstone Project
Learn how to design autonomous systems where multiple specialised agents collaborate under an orchestration layer that routes tasks, manages state, and handles failures.

School Name: The Engineering Summer School
Course Name: AI in Chemical Engineering: From Reactor to Refinery
Desc_short: AI is reshaping the future of Chemical Engineering. Explore how Artificial Intelligence is transforming industries through smarter reactors, optimized processes, advanced control systems, and data-driven refinery operations.
Desc: An introduction to the applications of AI in Chemical Engineering, covering process modeling, optimization, process control, and smart manufacturing. Learn how AI is transforming chemical plants, reactors, refineries, and industrial decision-making.
Certification: To be announced
Week 1: Week 1: Introduction to AI in Chemical Engineering. Explore the fundamentals of AI and machine learning, and discover how these technologies are transforming modern chemical engineering and process industries.
Week 2: Week 2: AI for Reactors and Process Modeling. Understand how AI can predict reactor performance, model complex chemical processes, and support data-driven decision-making in process engineering.
Week 3: Week 3: AI for Process Control and Optimization. Learn how AI can enhance process control, optimize operating conditions, and improve efficiency, safety, and performance in chemical plants.
Week 4: Week 4: AI in Refineries and Smart Manufacturing. Discover how AI is transforming refinery operations and smart manufacturing through predictive analytics, automation, and data-driven decision-making.

School Name: The Science Summer School (Pure Sciences like Maths, Biology, Physics, Chemistry, Economics*)
Course Name: Radioisotope Batteries and Hydrogen Fuel Cells in Space Applications
Desc_short: Explore the technologies that power space missions. From radioisotope batteries to hydrogen fuel cells, discover how nuclear chemistry and electrochemistry enable exploration beyond Earth.
Desc: Gain insights into the technologies that power space missions, exploring the science, applications, and future of radioisotope batteries and hydrogen fuel cells.
Certification: To be announced
Week 1: Week 1: The Space Power Problem. Learn why generating and storing energy in space is challenging, and explore the power requirements of modern space missions.
Week 2: Week 2: Radioisotope Batteries – Nuclear Heat at Work. Discover how nuclear energy is used to generate reliable power for spacecraft operating far from the Sun.
Week 3: Week 3: Hydrogen Fuel Cells – Chemistry That Powers Astronauts. Understand how hydrogen fuel cells generate clean and efficient energy, providing power and water for crewed space missions.
Week 4: Week 4: Head-to-Head – Choosing the Right Technology. Compare radioisotope batteries and hydrogen fuel cells, evaluating their advantages, limitations, and suitability for different space missions.
